transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I guess they wanted me to come in because of some stuff at work. I work at a freight warehouse, and... well, it’s really nothing bad, I promise, just maybe a little misunderstanding. I guess I keep doing things that bother the other guys. Like, sometimes I'll just sort of... freeze, with my arms up in the air by the forklift. 

And I've been copying the backing-up beeping sounds and the hand signals. I really thought I was just helping out, is that okay? But then I was moving the boxes into these... these strange little patterns. It made sense to me, but everyone was yelling at me to stop. I really didn't mean to cause any trouble or mess up the shift, I swear. Am I explaining this all right?
When you freeze like that, are you unable to move or speak even though you want to?

Oh, um... no, it's not like I'm trapped or paralyzed, I promise. I don't want you to think it's anything scary like that. I... I think I could move if I really tried. 

It's just, like I was saying before, when I keep doing those things—freezing with my arms up, or copying the beeping, or moving the boxes into those little patterns—it just feels like I'm supposed to do it right then. So I just stay like that. Even when everyone is yelling at me to stop, it's not that I can't hear them or can't speak, I just... I don't want to interrupt what I'm doing until it feels finished. I really don't mean to be a bad worker or ignore them. Is that... does that answer your question okay? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Have you had any times when you felt unusually energetic or unable to sleep, with your thoughts racing?

Oh, um, no... no, I don't think so. I usually sleep pretty okay, especially after a long shift at the warehouse. I get tired just like everyone else, so I don't really get super energetic or anything. I just try to be a steady worker, you know? 

And my thoughts, well, they just go at a normal speed, I think. I really hope that's the right answer. I'm not trying to be difficult or hold anything back from you, I promise, I just haven't really felt like that. Is it okay that I don't have that? I hope I'm still giving you the information you need.
Have you ever heard or seen things that other people around you could not?

No, I... I don't think I've ever had anything like that happen. I mean, the warehouse is really loud, so sometimes it's hard to hear people over the machines, but I've never heard anything that wasn't actually there, I promise. 

And I've never seen anything weird either. Just the normal stuff. I hope that's alright to say? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers. I really don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything like that. I'm just a normal guy trying to do my job, you know? Does that make sense?
Have you ever had a period when you strongly believed things that other people said were not true?

Oh, um, no, definitely not. I don't... I don't get into arguments with people about things like that. I really try to just get along with everyone at work and, you know, do what I'm supposed to do. 

If someone says something is a certain way, I just go with it. I wouldn't want to cause any trouble or make anyone think I'm being stubborn or... or weird. I just believe the normal things everyone else believes, I promise. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking? I hope I'm not misunderstanding you. I just really want to be helpful.
Before these episodes happen, do you feel an urge or tension that is relieved after you do the movement or sound?

Um, no, I... I don't really do any movements or sounds like that. I don't get any kind of tension or urge, either. I just... I just stand at my station and move the boxes like I'm supposed to. 

I try to stay really still and quiet when I'm not working, actually, so I don't bother anybody. I hope that's okay? I just wouldn't want anyone to think I was acting strange or doing things I couldn't control. I really try to be on my best behavior, I promise. Is it alright that I don't have those urges? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your notes.
Do you do the same movement or sound over and over in the same way, even when there’s no clear reason to?

No, no, I don't do anything like that. I don't repeat movements or make sounds over and over. I mean, at the warehouse, I do the same motions a lot, like lifting and stacking, but that's just the job, you know? There's a clear reason for it. 

But outside of work, or just sitting here? No, I don't have any strange habits or tics or anything. I try to be really mindful of how I act around other people. I wouldn't want to do something that looked odd or made anyone uncomfortable. I just try to act normal, like everyone else. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering these questions the right way for you. I just want to make sure I'm being a good patient.
When you freeze with your arms up, are you able to lower them if someone asks you to?

Um, well... I guess maybe sometimes I don't lower them right away. I don't mean to be disobedient, I promise! It's just... I guess that's why they brought me in here. At the warehouse, I've been doing this thing where I freeze with my arms up near the forklift. 

And, um, I guess I've been copying the beeping sounds it makes, and the hand signals the drivers use. And sometimes I arrange the boxes in these... these little patterns instead of just stacking them. Even when the supervisor is yelling at me to stop and get back to normal work. I don't know why I do it, it just happens. I'm really sorry if that sounds bad. I know I'm supposed to just do my job and listen. Does... does that make me a bad worker? I'm really trying my best to be good, I swear.
Do you ever repeat the same movement in a fixed, patterned way, like the same gesture or posture over and over?

Um... no, not really. I mean, besides what I just told you about the forklift signals... I don't think I do any other gestures or postures over and over. 

I really try to just keep my hands to myself and stand normally when I'm not working. I want to look professional, you know? I took some college classes a while back and I know how important it is to present yourself well, so I definitely try not to do anything that looks out of place or weird. 

I hope that's the right answer? I don't want you to think I'm holding anything back, I just really don't think I do that. I'm trying to be as helpful as I can with all your questions, I promise.
When someone tells you to stop or move your arms during one of these episodes, do you usually do the opposite of what they ask?

Oh, no, please don't think I'm doing it on purpose! I would never want to be defiant or do the opposite just to make people mad. I respect my bosses a lot. 

It's just... well, like I was saying, I guess that's really the main reason they brought me in here. When I'm at the warehouse freezing with my arms up by the forklift, or copying the beeping and the hand signals, or moving the boxes into those strange little patterns... even when everyone is yelling for me to stop and put my hands down, I just... I don't stop. 

It probably looks like I'm doing the exact opposite of what they ask, or just ignoring them, but I swear I'm not trying to be a bad employee or cause trouble. I really want to be cooperative and do what I'm told. Does that make sense? I hope you believe me, I really am trying to be good.
When these episodes happen, do you ever keep the same rigid posture for a long time, even if someone tries to move you?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I know I said I freeze up sometimes, but I wouldn't say I'm rigid, like, like a statue or anything. If someone really needed to move me, I'm sure I'd just let them. I wouldn't fight them on it. 

I really try not to be a bother to anyone, so I wouldn't want to make it hard for them to move me if I was in the way. I'm pretty flexible, you know? I definitely wouldn't just stand there stiffly if someone was trying to help me. I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I'm really trying to be a good patient.
Have these unusual movements and copying behaviors been present since childhood?

Oh, no, definitely not! Please don't think I've always been like this. I was a really good kid, I promise. I never did anything weird or caused any trouble for my parents or teachers growing up. 

Um... all of this, you know, the... the confusing talking and the strange behavior at the warehouse... it's really only been happening for about six months now. Just the last six months. So it's not like a lifelong problem or anything bad like that. I'm usually really normal and put-together, I swear. 

I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right timeline so I can be as helpful as possible. I really am trying my best to answer everything right for you.
Since these symptoms started, have you been functioning worse at work or in your daily life?

Um... I really try to keep up with everything, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm lazy or just giving up. But... well, I guess things have been a little bit harder lately. 

At work, they, um... they had me stop doing my forklift duties. Just for now, I think! And I've fallen a little behind in my community-college classes, but I'm planning to study extra hard to catch up, I really am. I also had to stop showing up for my volunteer shifts at the church food-bank... it's just, well, people started saying they couldn't really count on me right now, or that they couldn't keep things safe when I was around the equipment or the heavy boxes. 

Which I totally understand! I'd never want to put anyone in danger or be a bad worker. I hope you don't think less of me for all that... I really am trying my best to get back on track and be responsible. Did I answer that okay for you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
When you’re holding one of those poses, do you ever stay completely still for a long time, almost like your body is frozen in that position?

Oh, um, no, definitely not for a long time. I know I mentioned freezing up for just a second sometimes, but I never get stuck like that. I always snap right out of it, I promise. 

I wouldn't just stand there completely frozen for ages, that would be really strange and... and probably kind of creepy for other people to look at, wouldn't it? I really try to stay aware of what's going on around me so I don't bother anyone or look too out of place. I always make sure to keep moving if I need to. 

Is that what you needed to know? I hope I'm explaining it right for you. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the clearest answers I can.
Since these problems started, have you noticed becoming much less interested in things or having less emotion than you used to?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all! I still care about things, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around not caring or being cold to people. 

I mean, I know I had to step back from some things like the food bank and my classes, but that's just because I've been a little overwhelmed, not because I lost interest. I still have feelings and everything, just like normal. I still smile and... and get upset about things, you know? I'm not just blank. 

I always try to be polite and show people I care about what they're saying. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want to come across as uncaring or empty. Does that sound okay to you?
Since these problems started, have you had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually depressed?

Um, depressed? No, I... I really don't think so. I mean, I have days where I feel a little down or tired, but who doesn't, right? 

I definitely wouldn't say I've been unusually depressed or... or just lying in bed crying for days or anything like that. I really try to keep my chin up and stay positive, even with everything going on. I know people don't like being around someone who's always gloomy, so I make sure to put on a brave face and keep trying my best. 

I hope that's the right answer... I just don't want you to worry that I'm a danger to myself or completely falling apart. I'm really trying to stay strong. Did that make sense?
Have you ever felt that other people were watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm you?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, I know sometimes people just glance at each other, but I don't ever think anyone is actually watching me or plotting to hurt me or anything like that. That would be really scary, and... and I wouldn't want you to think I'm paranoid or suspicious of people. 

I always try to get along with everyone at the warehouse. I just put my head down, move the boxes, and do my work, you know? I really try to be friendly and helpful so no one would ever have any reason to say bad things about me behind my back. I trust people, I really do. 

Is that... is that the kind of answer you needed? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making it sound like I'm causing trouble with anyone.
Have you had any periods of feeling unusually elated or irritable for several days at a time?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I try really hard to keep a... an even temper, you know? I definitely don't get unusually irritable or angry at people for days. I'd feel just terrible if I acted like that or made anyone uncomfortable. 

And I don't get, like, super high or overly excited either. I just try to be steady and easygoing, especially at the warehouse. I really don't want to be someone who causes drama or snaps at people. I always want to be polite and do what I'm supposed to do. 

I hope I'm not coming across as someone who gets worked up easily? I really do try my best to be pleasant and cooperative with everybody. Does that... does that answer what you were looking for?
Since these problems started, have you become more socially withdrawn or less interested in doing things you used to enjoy?

Um, no... I don't think I've withdrawn at all. I mean, I still try to get out and do things. I definitely don't just hide away in my room or anything like that. I know it's important to be around people, so I make a real effort to talk to the guys at work during breaks, and... and I still like doing my usual hobbies. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm just giving up or isolating myself. I know people don't really like it when you push them away or act antisocial, so I always try to be available and, you know, keep a smile on my face. I really try to be a good friend.

I hope it's okay that I still try to keep busy like that? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right things to stay on track and be a normal, active person.
Have you had trouble keeping your thoughts organized so that your speech becomes hard for other people to follow?

Um, well... I try really hard to speak clearly. I know communication is super important, especially at the warehouse. I always want to make sure I'm giving the right information. 

Sometimes, though, I guess... well, like if the supervisor asks me which pallets are going on the truck, I start trying to explain the load sheet. But then, I don't know, my brain just sort of... I might accidentally mention my old house, or, um, fishing, or the boxes we used to pack for church. I just want to give them all the details so they have everything they need! But then sometimes they look a little confused, and I realize maybe I didn't make perfect sense. 

I don't do it on purpose, I promise. I really try to keep everything straight so I don't hold anyone up. I just get a little tangled up trying to be helpful. Is... is it okay that I get a little sidetracked sometimes? I'm really working on being more organized when I talk to people.
